extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers using NIH eRA IAR / eRA Commons to write and submit application critiques
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step instructions for accessing, completing, saving, editing, and submitting online critique templates in the IAR system; guidance emphasizes using the NOFO review criteria, entering strengths/weaknesses, and assigning scores. Covers UI elements, template variations, and workflow (draft → edit → submit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of NOFO review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Online critiques include review criteria from the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) used to submit the application so that reviewers have all the information in front of them while reviewing applications and writing their critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NOFO criteria are presented within the online critique template and should be used as the authoritative set of evaluation dimensions for the application. Ensure that your strengths/weaknesses and scores map to the NOFO-specified review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record strengths and weaknesses for each criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: For each listed review criterion (example given: Factor 1: Importance of Research (Significance and Innovation)), the reviewer enters the strengths and weaknesses in the provided fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write clear, criterion-specific statements of strengths and weaknesses in the corresponding text fields. Use the fields provided for each criterion rather than free-texting elsewhere so that comments align with scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign a score for each criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers choose a score from the left-hand dropdown menu (or score box) associated with each review criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the numeric/grade score that corresponds to your written assessment for that criterion. Newer templates may have the score box contained within the expandable criterion section; other templates may show score boxes outside the sections—ensure you select the appropriate control for that template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness checking / alerts for missing entries
rubrics_metrics.description: The online critique system alerts the reviewer to missing entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to system alerts to ensure all required fields and scores are completed before submitting. Use alerts as a checklist to avoid incomplete critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save draft and iterative workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers have the option to save a partially written critique and come back to finish and submit later by clicking the Save and Exit button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Save and Exit to preserve partially completed critiques. To resume, access the critique via Submit Critique from the List of My Assigned Applications or List of All Applications, click Edit when the critique opens in read-only mode, continue working, and then Submit when finished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit final critique via Submit button
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers are ready to submit, they click the Submit button at the top right-hand corner of the online critique screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only click Submit after all required scores and written critiques are completed. The Submit button location is at the top right of the Online Critique screen and reappears in the menu while completing the critique after clicking Edit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access requirement: appropriate IAR / eRA Commons login and role
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be logged into IAR via eRA Commons with appropriate role(s) to access, fill out, and submit online critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify you have the necessary eRA Commons account and role permissions before attempting to access the Online Critique screen. If you cannot access the critique, check your account roles and contact support or your institution's administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying meetings that use online critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: If a meeting is using online critiques, an Online Critique icon appears on the List of Meetings screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for the Online Critique icon on the List of Meetings to identify meetings using the online critique templates. Use the List of My Assigned Applications or List of All Applications screens and the three-dot dropdown menu to access Submit Critique for assigned applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of template variation
rubrics_metrics.description: As NIH transitions to new Online Critique templates, reviewers and review staff may see a mix of templates; some show the criterion/factor score boxes outside each criterion expandable section while newer templates contain the score boxes within the expandable sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When switching between templates, pay attention to where score controls and fields are located so you enter information in the correct place. The functional behavior (entering strengths/weaknesses and scores, saving drafts, submitting) is consistent, but UI layout may differ.
